solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Dog bags smell by empty bin — that’s a little graphic! (9)

indicatorNotes.bags: to bag something is to hold it, so the dog holds what follows
indicatorNotes.empty: an emptied word keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: to tail someone is to dog them, following closely
a hum is a bad smell

annotation.surface: A dog-walker bagging up a smelly deposit beside an emptied bin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal in a dog-walking scene; it is the verb, to follow closely. Hum is British slang for a bad smell.
annotation.definitionFit: A thumbnail is a small preview image on a screen.

entries.clue: You shouldn’t have cut short trip to fix wiper (5,3)

indicatorNotes.cut short: the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.to fix: the trip is fixed around the wiper, holding it

blocks.note: TOUR, a trip, without its last letter
a hanky is what you wipe your nose with

annotation.surface: A complaint that someone shortened a holiday just to repair a windscreen wiper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wiper' sits by 'fix' so a car comes to mind, but it is a handkerchief. The definition is a whole phrase, the polite thing said on receiving a gift.
annotation.definitionFit: 'You shouldn't have' is what people say to thank someone for a present.

entries.clue: University never involving a single constituent (5)

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university
nary is a dialect word for not one, never a

annotation.surface: A university that never takes in a single student.
annotation.walkthrough: NARY survives mostly in the phrase 'nary a word', meaning not a single word.
annotation.definitionFit: Unary means consisting of or acting on one element, as in a unary operation.

entries.clue: Criminal working to quash brand-new court proceedings (9)

indicatorNotes.to quash: the outer pair squashes the new piece between them

blocks.note: a bad lot is a criminal one
a machine that is on is working

annotation.surface: A crook's lawyer trying to get fresh legal proceedings thrown out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court proceedings' paints a trial; the court is a sports court and the proceedings are the game played on it.
annotation.definitionFit: The court is the one with a high net, and the proceedings are the shuttlecock rallies played across it.

entries.clue: Prickly young child disdainfully standing in corner (7)

indicatorNotes.standing: in a down answer, standing up means reading bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: the reversed piece goes inside the corner

blocks.note: calling a baby 'it' is a disdainful way to refer to it

annotation.surface: A sulky toddler sent to stand in the corner.
annotation.walkthrough: The naughty child in the corner is the whole scene, but the child is only the pronoun, the dismissive word for a baby.
annotation.definitionFit: Atingle means tingling, prickling with sensation.

entries.clue: Condition set out in support of album being flogged (7)

indicatorNotes.in support of: in a down answer, a support sits underneath
indicatorNotes.being flogged: beaten about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to set out is to go

annotation.surface: Terms laid down for promoting a record that is being sold hard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flogged' means sold in British slang, which suits the album; here it means beaten. 'Set out' looks like the anagram signal and is GO instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Lumbago is a medical condition, pain in the lower back.

entries.clue: Person preparing food’s left out pop (5)

indicatorNotes.left out: the L, for left, is taken out

blocks.note: a plater puts food on plates

annotation.surface: A cook who has forgotten the fizzy drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like soda in a kitchen scene; it is father, and PATER is the Latin word public-school English used for one.
annotation.definitionFit: Pater and pop are both informal words for father.

entries.clue: God Risen, part of Bible Camp drama (5)

indicatorNotes.Risen: in a down answer, rising means reading bottom to top

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
OT = Old Testament, reversed to TO

annotation.surface: A Bible camp putting on an Easter play about the risen Christ.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bible Camp' pairs the two words, but 'Camp' belongs with 'drama'. A panto is a British Christmas pantomime, a riotously camp family show.
annotation.definitionFit: Pantomime is famously camp, with cross-dressing dames and slapstick.

entries.clue: “T” in rank when it’s bordering last quarter of alphabet (9)

annotation.definition: “T” in rank when it’s bordering last quarter of alphabet

indicatorNotes.rank: rank means foul or corrupted, so the letters are spoiled into a new order
indicatorNotes.bordering: the outer letters border the inserted pair

blocks.note: ALPHABET has eight letters; its last two are ET

annotation.surface: A question of where the letter T stands in the alphabet.
annotation.walkthrough: T does double duty on purpose: the letter defined and a letter of the fodder. 'Last quarter of alphabet' tempts you toward the letters T to Z; it means the last quarter of the word ALPHABET.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the whole clue is true: T is twentieth in the alphabet, just inside its last quarter.

entries.clue: Pope could be concerned with goodness hour on end (6)

indicatorNotes.on end: stood on end in a down answer, the letters read upwards

blocks.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour

annotation.surface: A pontiff devoting an hour to the question of goodness.
annotation.walkthrough: Pope is Alexander Pope, the 18th-century poet famous for rhyming couplets, not the head of the Catholic church.
annotation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope wrote in rhyme, so he could be called a rhymer.

entries.clue: Right to plug A Fistful of Dollars for one commendation? (5)

indicatorNotes.to plug: a plug fills a hole, so R goes inside

blocks.clueFragment: A Fistful of Dollars for one
blocks.note: a wad is a thick fistful of banknotes

annotation.surface: A plug for the Clint Eastwood western as prize material.
annotation.walkthrough: The film title is taken literally: a fistful of dollars is a wad of cash.
annotation.definitionFit: A commendation is a formal mark of praise, and a prize or medal is the tangible form it takes.

entries.clue: Jolly fellows sporting smiley masks (9)

indicatorNotes.sporting: playing about, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.masks: the outer letters mask what they cover

annotation.surface: Cheerful chaps wearing grinning face masks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like the cheerful fellows; it is the British intensifier, as in jolly good.
annotation.definitionFit: In British speech jolly means very, as does immensely.

entries.clue: Band for opening act? (3,4)

blocks.note: surface: a group of musicians; meant: a circle of metal
surface: the support slot before the headliner; meant: what unlocks a door

annotation.surface: A group booked to warm up the crowd before the headliner.
annotation.walkthrough: The band and the opening act are both music terms; read literally, the band is a hoop and the opening is done by what hangs on it.
annotation.definitionFit: A key ring is a metal band holding the keys you open doors with.

entries.clue: Person looking to save pale ale bottles (7)

indicatorNotes.bottles: to bottle something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: a pale is a fence stake, a post

annotation.surface: A drinker keeping pale ale to one side for later.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pale ale' is a real beer, so the words fuse; pale is a stake, as in 'beyond the pale'.
annotation.definitionFit: An apostle is a missionary seeking to save souls.

entries.clue: Plain green tracker jackets sold directly (4-3-7)

indicatorNotes.jackets: a jacket wraps around, so the tracker encloses green

annotation.surface: A shop selling plain green hunting jackets straight off the shelf.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word looks like clothing catalogue copy; 'Plain' and 'green' are separate pieces, not one description.
annotation.definitionFit: Over-the-counter goods are sold directly to the customer, especially medicines needing no prescription.

entries.clue: Unusually, taxes due around end of month all in (9)

indicatorNotes.Unusually: the letters appear in an unusual order
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around the H

annotation.surface: Exceptionally high tax bills arriving at month's end, leaving you spent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'All in' is British for worn out, which fits someone flattened by a tax bill.
annotation.definitionFit: All in and exhausted both mean completely tired.

entries.clue: Knight with virtue delaying married routine (9)

indicatorNotes.delaying: the letter is held back, appearing later in the word

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for knight
MORALITY, virtue, with its M for married moved back

annotation.surface: A virtuous knight putting off his wedding.
annotation.walkthrough: M is the abbreviation for married; it slides from the front of the virtue to third place.
annotation.definitionFit: Normality is the usual routine state of things.

entries.clue: Small power boat on lake flipped over rock? (8)

indicatorNotes.flipped over: turned upside down in a down answer, so read upwards

blocks.note: RE = on, about, flipped to ER

annotation.surface: A little motorboat capsizing on a rock in a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: The rock looks like the thing the boat hits; it is slang for a diamond.
annotation.definitionFit: Sparkler and rock are both slang for a diamond.

entries.clue: Position new instrument aboard tea clipper? (14)

indicatorNotes.aboard: on board a ship, so inside the vessel

blocks.note: char is British slang for tea
a cello is a string instrument
a clipper is a fast sailing ship

annotation.surface: Stowing a brand-new instrument on one of the old tea clippers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tea clipper' is a real kind of ship, so it reads as one; here tea and clipper are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Position in the sense of a post held, as in 'a position in the firm'; this one is a chancellor's office.

entries.clue: Copper perhaps exposed clientele — men typically (7)

indicatorNotes.exposed: the answer is laid bare inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A shop's customer base shown up as mostly male.
annotation.walkthrough: Copper looks like slang for a policeman; it is the metal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: copper is one entry in the periodic table, number 29.

entries.clue: Flying solo, the African lands in high place (7)

indicatorNotes.Flying: letters sent flying land in a new order

annotation.surface: A lone pilot touching down on a high African airstrip.
annotation.walkthrough: Lesotho is a small mountain kingdom surrounded by South Africa; all of it lies above 1,000 metres, the highest low point of any country.
annotation.definitionFit: Lesotho is an African country set entirely at high altitude.

entries.clue: Mother very upset to admit one’s 18 (6)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down
indicatorNotes.to admit: to let in, so the I goes inside

annotation.surface: A mother very distressed at confessing her child is eighteen.
annotation.walkthrough: 18 points to the answer at 18 down, and osmium is one of those. The age reading, a mother upset that her child is eighteen, is the trap.
annotation.definitionFit: Osmium is a chemical element, a dense blue-grey metal, which is what 18 down names.

entries.clue: Short piece replacing one of magnitude in press (7)

indicatorNotes.Short: the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.replacing: the new piece takes the place of the letter named

blocks.note: QUEEN, a chess piece, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A brief newspaper item standing in for an important story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece' and 'press' suggest journalism; the piece is a chess queen, and press is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to press something and to squeeze it both mean to push hard on it from the sides.

entries.clue: No head on Guinness? That is strangely disturbing (5)

annotation.surface: A drinker unsettled by a pint of Guinness with no creamy head.
annotation.walkthrough: A pint of Guinness without its foam head would look wrong to anyone who knows the stout; here the head is just a first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange in a way that disturbs.

entries.clue: Strip off blind woman’s coat (7)

blocks.note: a slat is a strip from a Venetian blind

annotation.surface: Taking the coat off a woman who cannot see.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strip off' reads as undressing and 'blind' as sightless; the strip is a slat from a window blind, and coat is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Coat is a verb here: to spread something thickly over a surface, like butter on toast.

entries.clue: Ungulate with aquatic habits in river (5)

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

annotation.surface: A hoofed animal that likes to wallow in rivers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In river' reads as where the animal lives; the 'in' is a word for fashionable.
annotation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is a hoofed mammal that spends its days in water.

entries.clue: Break in black bears caught by team in Italy (9)

indicatorNotes.bears: to bear is to carry, so black holds the C

annotation.surface: Black-clad Italian fans breaking in and grabbing some bears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Break in' looks like burglary; it means interrupt. Inter is the Milan football club.
annotation.definitionFit: Break in as in interrupting a conversation: throwing a remark in while others are talking.

entries.clue: Force short confession from Brazilian striker? (5)

indicatorNotes.short: the phrase loses its last letter

blocks.note: what Brazil's great striker might own up to: I'M PELE

annotation.surface: Squeezing an admission out of a Brazilian footballer.
annotation.walkthrough: The confession is the great Brazilian forward admitting who he is, docked its final E.
annotation.definitionFit: To impel is to force or drive someone to act.

entries.clue: Detective circled by for one mile after reversing Mini Minor? (5)

indicatorNotes.circled: gone round, so the letters turn back

annotation.surface: A police chase in a Mini going round in circles.
annotation.walkthrough: The Mini Minor was a classic small British car; read as two words, a tiny minor is a midge, the smallest of insects.
annotation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny insect, or informally a very small person.

entries.clue: Length of timber that could make a cube (3-2-4)

blocks.note: a standard sawn plank, named for its cross-section in inches
two times four makes eight, and eight is two cubed

annotation.surface: A carpenter eyeing a plank to cut into blocks.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is arithmetic: the product is eight, a cube number.
annotation.definitionFit: A two-by-four is a standard length of sawn timber, two inches by four.
